trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Haruka Express train from Kansai International Airport to Kyoto Station (approx. 75 min, ~¥1,800 with IC card). Budget tip: buy an ICOCA card at the airport for seamless transit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Once settled, take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park itself — Japan's most famous cherry blossom park is steps from your door. In late April some late-blooming varieties may still be visible. Explore the stone lantern paths and the iconic weeping cherry tree (Gion Shidare-zakura). Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, lined with traditional wooden machiya shops. Browse local crafts and snacks. End the evening with a casual dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab an onigiri (¥120–¥180) and green tea at a 7-Eleven or Lawson convenience store at the airport.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bento box at Kyoto Station's underground food hall (Porta or The Cube) — hearty options from ¥500–¥900.
meals.dinner: Ramen at Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station — bowls from ¥850–¥1,100. Easy walk back to hotel via taxi or bus.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to travel fatigue. Keep the evening short. Get your ICOCA card loaded with at least ¥3,000 for the first few days of transit. April 15 in Kyoto typically has mild temperatures (14–20°C) — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free sunrise walk through Maruyama Park before crowds arrive — magical atmosphere with cherry blossoms and temple bells. Then visit Yasaka Shrine (free entry, open 24 hrs) adjacent to the park. Head uphill to Chion-in Temple (free grounds, ¥500 for inner sanctuary) — one of Japan's most impressive temple gates (sanmon).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to Kiyomizudera Temple (¥400 entry). The wooden stage platform offers sweeping views over Kyoto and surrounding hillside cherry blossoms. Explore the Otowa waterfall and three streams (love, longevity, success). Descend via Kiyomizu-zaka shopping street for matcha soft serve (¥350–¥500).
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the heart of Gion district at dusk — the best time to spot maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to evening engagements along Hanamikoji Street. Window-shop and photograph the preserved ochaya (teahouse) facades. Free activity.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a morning set (tamago sando + coffee) from a nearby FamilyMart for ~¥350, or try Inoda Coffee Sanjo — a Kyoto institution with morning sets from ¥750.
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine at Okutan Kiyomizu near the temple — a budget-friendly tofu kaiseki set from ¥1,500, or grab yudofu (tofu hot pot) from a street vendor for ¥600.
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market evening stroll — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' — sample street food: grilled skewers (¥150–¥300 each), tamagoyaki, pickles. Make a light dinner of market tastings for under ¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant uphill walking. Kiyomizudera is busiest 10am–3pm; arriving at opening (6am) is ideal but afternoon is fine. Keep receipts for temple entries to track budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take Bus 59 or 26 to Arashiyama (30–40 min, ¥230 with ICOCA). Visit the iconic Bamboo Grove — free and stunning in morning light before tour groups arrive. Walk to Tenryuji Temple garden (¥500) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with a pond garden backed by forested mountains. Cherry blossoms may still linger on the hillside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River — a classic Kyoto scene. Rent a rowboat (¥1,500/30 min for up to 3 people) for a unique family perspective. Explore Jojakko-ji or Nison-in temple on the hillside (¥400–¥500 each) for quieter, less-crowded blossom viewing. Visit Okochi Sanso Villa garden (¥1,000 includes matcha tea) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area by bus. Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha (free, open 24 hrs) — take Bus 5 from Gion. Walk the first 20–30 minutes up the torii gate tunnel path at dusk for an otherworldly atmosphere. Return to hotel by 9pm.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel (¥300–¥400) or grab fresh yudofu from a Arashiyama vendor on arrival.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama has many budget options — try Yoshimura for soba noodles (¥900–¥1,200) or grab a packed lunch from a convenience store to eat by the river (¥500–¥700).
meals.dinner: Gyukatsu Motomura near Kyoto Station (10-min bus ride) — crispy beef cutlet set meal ¥1,200–¥1,500, very filling and popular with families.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday will be busier — arrive at Arashiyama before 9am if possible. Fushimi Inari is a 15-minute train ride from Kyoto Station (JR Nara Line, ¥150) or take the bus from Gion. The full Inari hike takes 2–3 hrs but the lower section is enough for an evening visit with children.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a 2km canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees (some late bloomers likely still present in mid-April). Walk from Ginkakuji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500) southward. The path is free and one of Kyoto's most beloved spring walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nanzenji Temple complex (free grounds, ¥600 for main hall). The massive sanmon gate and red-brick aqueduct are iconic. Walk to nearby Heian Jingu Shrine (free exterior, ¥600 for garden) — the garden is spectacular in spring with weeping cherry trees and wisteria beginning to bloom.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Maruyama Park for an evening picnic under the illuminated cherry trees (if still blooming). Many locals bring convenience store snacks and sit on blue tarps — join in! This is a quintessential Japanese hanami (flower viewing) experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Omen Noodles near Ginkakuji — hearty udon sets from ¥900 (opens 11am, so grab a convenience store snack first if walking early).
meals.lunch: Picnic along Philosopher's Path — buy onigiri, tamagoyaki, and drinks from a Lawson or 7-Eleven for ~¥600–¥800 total.
meals.dinner: Supermarket deli dinner — visit Fressay or Izumiya supermarket near the hotel for half-price bento boxes after 7pm (¥300–¥500). Great budget strategy for families.

day_by_day.notes: Sunday crowds at Philosopher's Path and Nanzenji can be heavy — start by 8:30am. Heian Jingu holds the Jidai Matsuri (Festival of Ages) in October, but April often has smaller cultural events — check local listings. The evening Maruyama Park hanami is a highlight that families love.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min by Kintetsu Express from Kyoto Station, ¥680 one way). Arrive at Nara Park — home to over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer. Children absolutely love feeding them shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack sold at stands). Visit Todaiji Temple (¥600) — housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine (free exterior, ¥500 for inner sanctuary) — famous for its thousands of bronze and stone lanterns. Walk through the forested Kasugayama Primeval Forest path (free) connecting the shrine to Nigatsu-do Hall with panoramic views over Nara.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by 6pm. Relax in the hotel and explore the quiet evening lanes of Gion. Visit a sento (public bathhouse) — Funaoka Onsen in Kyoto is a historic option (¥500 entry) for a cultural soak after a long walking day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or convenience store before catching the train (¥300–¥400).
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — a Nara specialty. Try Hiraso restaurant near Todaiji (~¥1,200) or buy a box from a station vendor (¥800).
meals.dinner: Back in Kyoto — try Ippudo Ramen on Kawaramachi (¥900–¥1,100 per bowl) or a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Musashi Sushi near Nishiki Market (¥110–¥165 per plate).

day_by_day.notes: Monday is a good day to visit Nara as crowds are lighter than weekends. Warn children that deer can be pushy when they see the crackers — hold bags close! Kintetsu Express is faster and more comfortable than JR for Nara; buy tickets at Kyoto Station's Kintetsu entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka (30 min by Hankyu or JR from Kyoto, ¥560–¥580). Head to Osaka Castle (¥600 museum entry, park free) — one of Japan's most iconic landmarks with excellent cherry blossom grounds. The castle park has over 600 cherry trees and the moat reflections are stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Dotonbori — Osaka's neon-lit entertainment district. Walk along the canal, see the famous Glico Running Man sign, and explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade. Visit the free Hozenji Yokocho alley — a tiny atmospheric lane with moss-covered stone lanterns.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Osaka's legendary food culture — 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop). Takoyaki (octopus balls) at Wanaka (¥600/8 pieces), Okonomiyaki at Mizuno (¥900–¥1,400), or street gyoza. Return to Kyoto by 9–10pm via Hankyu or JR.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or quick stand near Kyoto Station before departing.
meals.lunch: Osaka's famous 551 Horai pork buns (nikuman) near Dotonbori — ¥200 each, iconic and delicious. Grab 2–3 for a filling lunch under ¥600.
meals.dinner: Dotonbori street food crawl — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person for a mix of takoyaki, okonomiyaki, and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). Extremely fun for families.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is an easy and highly recommended day trip from Kyoto. The Hankyu Kyoto Line from Kawaramachi Station to Umeda (Osaka) is slightly cheaper than JR. Keep your ICOCA card loaded. Dotonbori is safe and very family-friendly in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore northern Kyoto — take Bus 101 or 205 to Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion, ¥400). The gold-leaf-covered pavilion reflected in its mirror pond is breathtaking. Arrive early (opens 9am) to beat crowds. Nearby Ryoanji Temple (¥600) features Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — a meditative and culturally rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nishiki Tenmangu Shrine (free) hidden inside Nishiki Market arcade — a quirky, beloved local shrine. Then spend the afternoon at the Kyoto International Manga Museum (¥900 adults, ¥400 children) — a former school converted into a manga library with 300,000 volumes. Kids and adults love it. Great rainy-day backup too.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pontocho Alley at dusk — a narrow lantern-lit lane parallel to the Kamo River, lined with restaurants. More atmospheric than dining — walk through and choose a budget izakaya. Sit along the Kamo River on the wooden platforms (kawayuka) if weather permits.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local kissaten (old-school Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel — toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥700.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market food stalls — try fresh tofu, pickles, and skewered food for a market lunch under ¥800.
meals.dinner: Pontocho izakaya — look for set menus (teishoku) at standing bars or smaller places; budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person including a drink. Ganko Sushi on Sanjo has great value sets.

day_by_day.notes: Kinkakuji is one of Japan's most visited sites — Wednesday morning is calmer than weekends. The Manga Museum is a genuine cultural institution, not just a tourist gimmick — highly recommended for families with children. Pontocho is narrow; strollers may be difficult.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha properly (free, open 24 hrs) — take Bus 5 from Gion or JR from Kyoto Station (¥150). Hike the full Senbon Torii (thousand torii gate) trail to the summit (2–3 hours round trip, 233m elevation). Spectacular views and far fewer crowds above the first viewpoint. A genuine adventure for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit nearby Fushimi Sake District — Fushimi is one of Japan's top sake-producing regions. Walk along the willow-lined Benten Canal and visit Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum (¥600, includes sake tasting for adults) — educational and fun. The historic brewery buildings are beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto central. Visit Nishiki Market for final souvenir shopping (closes around 6pm for most shops). Spend a quiet final full evening in Gion — walk Shirakawa Canal path, lined with cherry trees and stone lanterns, for a romantic and memorable evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Onigiri and miso soup from convenience store (¥300–¥400) — eat before the Inari hike.
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (fox sushi — fried tofu pouches filled with rice) is the traditional local food of Fushimi Inari. Buy a pack from a street vendor at the shrine base (¥300–¥500) — delicious and culturally appropriate.
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu Daruma — a beloved Osaka-style kushikatsu chain with a Kyoto branch. Sets from ¥1,200. Family-friendly with fun dipping sauce rules ('no double dipping!').

day_by_day.notes: The full Fushimi Inari hike is manageable for most children (ages 6+) but can be tiring — bring water and snacks. The Fushimi sake district is a 10-minute walk from Fushimi Inari Station (Kintetsu line). Shirakawa Canal evening walk is one of Kyoto's most underrated experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Daitokuji Temple complex in northern Kyoto (Bus 205, ¥230) — a vast Zen temple complex with 22 sub-temples, several open to the public (¥400–¥600 each). Daisen-in sub-temple has outstanding dry landscape gardens. Far less crowded than mainstream sites — a true cultural gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Kyoto Railway Museum (¥1,200 adults, ¥500 children) — an outstanding museum with 53 real locomotives, a working steam locomotive ride (¥300 extra), and interactive exhibits. Extremely popular with children and families. Located near Kyoto Station (15-min walk or Bus 205).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening souvenir shopping at Kyoto Station's underground mall (Porta) and department store basement (depachika) — stock up on matcha sweets, yatsuhashi (Kyoto's famous cinnamon rice cake), and packaged foods as gifts. Grab a memorable last dinner near the station.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby kissaten. Treat yourself to a proper sit-down morning meal on this penultimate day (¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Kyoto Railway Museum has a restaurant shaped like a dining car — fun for kids. Budget set meals ¥900–¥1,200. Alternatively, bring convenience store lunches to eat in the museum's outdoor area.
meals.dinner: Kyoto Station Isetan 11th floor restaurant strip — wide variety of options. Try Kyoto-style kaiseki at a budget kaiseki restaurant (lunch menus are cheaper; dinner sets from ¥1,500–¥2,500). Alternatively, splurge slightly on your last night at a nicer izakaya.

day_by_day.notes: Daitokuji is a wonderful off-the-beaten-path experience — the sub-temple gardens rival Ryoanji but with almost no crowds. The Railway Museum is a genuine highlight for children and worth the entry price. Book online in advance if possible to save queuing time.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake early for one last sunrise walk through Maruyama Park. Take photos of the weeping cherry tree and Yasaka Shrine pagoda. Visit any missed local spots or revisit a favorite. Check out of hotel by 11am (confirm checkout time with hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Kansai International Airport (KIX) via Haruka Express from Kyoto Station (~75 min, ¥1,800). Arrive at airport 2–3 hours before departure. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Japanese snacks, cosmetics, or souvenirs (often cheaper than city shops).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of cherry blossoms, culture, and family memories across Kyoto, Nara, and Osaka.

meals.breakfast: Final convenience store breakfast or a bowl of Kyoto-style obanzai (small vegetable dishes) at a local morning restaurant near Maruyama Park (¥600–¥900).
meals.lunch: Kyoto Station Cube food hall — grab ekiben (station bento boxes, ¥900–¥1,400) to eat on the Haruka Express. A classic Japanese travel tradition.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at KIX — options range from ramen (¥900) to sushi sets (¥1,200–¥1,800). Alternatively, eat your ekiben on the train and have a light airport snack.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time on Saturday morning — Kyoto Station is busier on weekends. Return your ICOCA card at any JR green window to reclaim your ¥500 deposit (minus ¥220 handling fee) — worth doing if you have time. Keep ¥1,000–¥2,000 in cash for airport transport and final expenses. Sayonara and safe travels!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel to accommodation in Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, freshen up, then take a gentle stroll through Maruyama Park to see the iconic weeping cherry tree and soak in the hanami atmosphere. The park is steps from the hotel — perfect for a low-key first afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka nearby, lined with traditional shops and lanterns. End the evening with a relaxed walk through Gion's Hanamikoji Street hoping to spot a geiko or maiko.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip — arriving at 13:00
meals.lunch: Pick up a bento box or onigiri from a convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) near the hotel after check-in — quick, affordable, and authentically Japanese (¥500–¥800)
meals.dinner: Omen Kodaiji — a beloved Kyoto noodle restaurant near Gion serving hearty udon in a cozy, traditional setting. Budget approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 1.5–2 hours for travel from Kansai International Airport to Kyoto Station via the Haruka Express (approx. ¥3,600), then a short taxi or bus to Maruyama Park. Keep Day 1 light to recover from jet lag. Cherry blossoms in mid-April may be in late bloom — check real-time forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Experience a full hanami morning under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to enjoy the park before crowds build. Walk to nearby Yasaka Shrine for a cultural bonus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Fushimi Inari Taisha (30 min by bus/train from Gion) and walk through the thousands of vermilion torii gates. Families can hike as far as comfortable — even the first 20 minutes offers stunning photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion district and enjoy the twilight illumination of Maruyama Park's cherry trees, which are often lit up beautifully after dark during blossom season.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) such as Inoda Coffee — a Kyoto institution. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Teahouse snack stalls inside Maruyama Park or near Fushimi Inari — try kitsune udon or inari sushi (fox sushi), thematically fitting for the shrine. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa — a friendly, mid-range izakaya in the Gion area offering a wide variety of Japanese small plates. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free to enter. Fushimi Inari is also free and open 24/7. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Fushimi Inari. The evening illumination in Maruyama Park is a must-see during cherry blossom season — typically runs until 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park — Take the Randen tram or bus to Arashiyama (approx. 30–40 min from Gion). Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves early in the morning when it is less crowded. Stroll along the Oi River and visit Tenryu-ji Temple garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (approx. 20-min uphill walk) where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids and adults alike will love feeding the monkeys from inside a small hut. Afterward, explore Arashiyama's charming shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion and enjoy a traditional kaiseki-style dinner to celebrate your first full cultural day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local bakery such as Sizuya Bakery in Kyoto — famous for their Katsu Sando. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama Yoshimura — a soba restaurant with stunning views of the Oi River and Togetsukyo Bridge. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Roan — an approachable kaiseki restaurant in the Higashiyama area near Gion, offering set menus that introduce traditional Kyoto cuisine. Budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Iwatayama Monkey Park admission: ¥550 for adults, ¥250 for children. Tenryu-ji Temple garden admission: ¥500. Arashiyama can get very crowded on weekends — arrive at the bamboo grove by 8:00–8:30 AM for the best experience. Strollers may be difficult on the monkey park trail.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Higashiyama Cultural District on foot — starting from your hotel, walk north through Chion-in Temple, Shoren-in Temple, and Heian Shrine. The wide tree-lined avenues and traditional architecture make this a quintessential Kyoto cultural morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kyoto National Museum (open Tuesday–Sunday) for a family-friendly deep dive into Japanese art, history, and culture. The Heisei Chishinkan Wing by I.M. Pei houses rotating special exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Evening free for independent exploration — browse the Nishiki Market (Kyoto's Kitchen) before it closes around 18:00, then enjoy a casual dinner in the Kawaramachi/Gion area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Kyoto-style morning tofu set (yudofu) at Tousuiro near Maruyama Park — a gentle, healthy start. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800.
meals.lunch: Cafe inside Heian Shrine garden or a picnic from Nishiki Market stalls — try grilled skewers, pickles, and fresh mochi. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Mishima-tei — a historic sukiyaki restaurant in the Kawaramachi area, a beloved Kyoto institution since 1873. Budget ¥3,500–¥5,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kyoto National Museum admission: approx. ¥700 for adults, free for children under 18. Heian Shrine garden admission: ¥600. The Nishiki Market is best visited in the afternoon before stalls close. Sunday can be busy — book dinner in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima — depart early from Kyoto Station via Shinkansen (approx. 1 hr 45 min, ¥5,720 one way). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park. This is a deeply moving and important cultural experience for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Hiroshima, take the JR San'yo Line to Miyajimaguchi (30 min) and then a short ferry to Miyajima Island (10 min). See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine, meet the friendly wild deer, and explore the island's shrines and pagodas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen, arriving by 20:00–21:00. Quiet dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast or hotel breakfast before departing — aim to leave Kyoto by 7:30–8:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki at Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) — a multi-floor building in Hiroshima dedicated entirely to this local specialty. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Ramen Kaikan near Kyoto Station or a simple bowl of ramen at Ippudo — a satisfying, low-effort dinner after a long day. Budget ¥900–¥1,400.

day_by_day.notes: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum admission: ¥200 for adults, free for children. Itsukushima Shrine admission: ¥300. The floating torii gate view depends on tides — check tide tables in advance for the best experience. This day involves significant walking and emotional content — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. A JR Pass will cover all Shinkansen and ferry costs on this route.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long Day 5 trip. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast, then take a peaceful morning walk through Maruyama Park and up to Kiyomizudera Temple (20-min walk from hotel). The temple's wooden stage offers sweeping views over Kyoto.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kiyomizudera's surrounding streets — Chawanzaka (Teapot Lane) and Sannen-zaka — browsing pottery, matcha sweets, and traditional crafts. Visit Kodai-ji Temple with its beautiful Zen garden, just a short walk away.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Gion Corner cultural performance (if available in April) showcasing tea ceremony, ikebana, koto music, and maiko dance — an ideal family cultural experience just minutes from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Slow hotel breakfast or a matcha parfait and toast at % Arabica Kyoto Higashiyama — a beautifully designed specialty coffee shop near the hotel. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Kasagi-ya — a tiny, beloved traditional sweet shop near Ninenzaka serving anmitsu and zenzai (sweet red bean desserts) — a delightful and affordable Kyoto lunch experience. Budget ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Gion Nanba — a refined but accessible Kyoto-style restaurant in the Gion area serving seasonal Japanese cuisine. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kiyomizudera admission: ¥500. Kodai-ji Temple admission: ¥600. Gion Corner performances typically cost ¥3,150 per person — book in advance at their website. The walk from the hotel to Kiyomizudera is uphill but manageable for families. This is a gentler day intentionally placed after the demanding Day 5.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo by Shinkansen Nozomi (approx. 2 hrs 15 min from Kyoto Station, ¥13,320 one way). Check in to a mid-range hotel in the Shinjuku or Shibuya area. Head to Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden for cherry blossom viewing — a large, family-friendly park with multiple blossom varieties that often bloom later than Kyoto's.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku — walk down Takeshita Street with the kids for quirky fashion and crepes, then stroll through the serene Meiji Shrine forest for a cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing experience. Observe from the Starbucks overlooking the crossing or walk through it yourself. Explore Shibuya's vibrant evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kyoto Station before boarding — Kyoto Station has excellent ekiben (station bento boxes) and bakeries. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen using food from nearby convenience stores or the park's own restaurant — a relaxed family lunch under cherry trees. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Ichiran Ramen in Shibuya — the famous solo-booth tonkotsu ramen chain, a uniquely Japanese dining experience loved by families and solo diners alike. Budget ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen admission: ¥500 for adults, free for children under 15. Meiji Shrine is free to enter. Book Tokyo hotel in advance — mid-April is peak cherry blossom season and accommodation fills up quickly. Consider Shinjuku, Shibuya, or Asakusa areas for convenient access to Day 8 activities. Note: alcohol is not permitted in Shinjuku Gyoen.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Take the metro to Tsukiji and explore the bustling outer market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), grilled scallops, and matcha soft serve. This is a fantastic sensory experience for families and food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Immerse your family in the breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations at teamLab Borderless (check current location — as of 2024 it relocated to Azabudai Hills). Allow 2–3 hours to fully explore the immersive rooms. Book tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Odaiba waterfront for stunning views of Tokyo Bay and the Rainbow Bridge at night. Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a life-size Gundam statue) or simply enjoy the illuminated waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: The Tsukiji Outer Market IS breakfast — graze through the stalls from 8:00–9:30 AM. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a full market tasting experience.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near teamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills — the complex has multiple mid-range dining options. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.
meals.dinner: Decks Tokyo Beach food court on Odaiba — a casual, family-friendly multi-cuisine food hall with great bay views. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person.

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets: approx. ¥3,200 for adults, ¥1,000 for children — MUST be booked online in advance as they sell out weeks ahead. Tsukiji Outer Market is most lively between 7:00–11:00 AM. The market is free to explore. Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome monorail — a fun ride for kids with great views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Visit Senso-ji Temple (Tokyo's oldest and most significant Buddhist temple), walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional souvenirs, and explore the surrounding Edo-era streetscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short walk to the Tokyo Skytree (634m — the world's tallest tower). Head up to the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo. Alternatively, visit the Sumida Aquarium at the base of the tower for a family-friendly afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — head to Akihabara (Electric Town) for a unique cultural experience browsing electronics, anime, manga, and retro game shops. A fascinating and distinctly Japanese experience for all ages.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a classic Japanese morning set at a kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near your hotel — coffee, toast, boiled egg, and salad. Budget ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan — a historic sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji, offering affordable lunch sets. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Akihabara has a range of themed restaurants — try a maid cafe for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience, or opt for a reliable kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) chain such as Sushiro for a fun family dinner. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji Temple is free to enter and open 24/7. Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck admission: ¥2,100 for adults, ¥950 for children. Sumida Aquarium: ¥2,300 for adults, ¥1,200 for children. Nakamise Shopping Street is ideal for last-minute souvenir shopping. Akihabara is best experienced in the evening when all the neon signs are illuminated.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — visit Ueno Park for a last cherry blossom stroll (late-blooming varieties may still be out in late April). The park also houses the Tokyo National Museum, the Tokyo Zoo (great for families), and several other museums if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, do final souvenir shopping in Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market with great deals on food, clothing, and goods. Head to the airport with ample time: Narita (60–90 min by Narita Express) or Haneda (30–45 min by monorail/train).
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final Japanese breakfast set — enjoy tamago gohan (raw egg on rice), miso soup, and grilled fish at a local teishoku restaurant. Budget ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — gyoza, takoyaki, fresh fruit, and snacks while browsing the stalls. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent Japanese restaurant options including ramen, sushi, and tempura. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for airport check-in, security, and immigration. Store luggage at the hotel until departure using the concierge service. Ueno Zoo admission: ¥600 for adults, ¥200 for children. Tokyo National Museum admission: ¥1,000. Consider purchasing airport transfer tickets the night before to avoid morning queues. A 10-day Suica or Pasmo IC card will have covered most of your Tokyo transit needs — check the remaining balance and use it up at convenience stores or vending machines before departing.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree in Maruyama Park. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the sakura season, and enjoy traditional street food stalls lining the park. Ideal for families with open lawns and a festive atmosphere.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's iconic Tsukiji Outer Market and sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha treats, and street snacks. A hands-on culinary adventure that introduces the whole family to authentic Japanese flavors and food culture in a vibrant, bustling setting.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations at teamLab Borderless. Children and adults alike are captivated by the luminous, ever-changing environments that blend technology and nature. A uniquely Japanese fusion of art, culture, and innovation.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama and then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids love feeding the monkeys while parents enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. A perfect blend of nature and family fun.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a culturally enriching day trip from Kyoto or Osaka to visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park, then ferry over to Miyajima Island to see the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Deer roam freely on the island, delighting children. A deeply meaningful and memorable cultural experience for the whole family.
experiences.location: Hiroshima Peace Park & Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transfer from airport to Kyoto via Haruka Express or private luxury car service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Freshen up and take a leisurely first stroll through Maruyama Park to see the iconic weeping cherry tree (Gion Shidare-zakura) in the late afternoon light. Enjoy the relaxed hanami atmosphere with lantern-lit paths.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle walk through the stone-lantern-lined lanes of Gion, Kyoto's famous geisha district. Explore Hanamikoji Street and enjoy the atmospheric twilight ambiance. Early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on board flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or bento box at Kyoto Station upon arrival — try Kyoto Cuisine Bento from the Isetan department store food hall
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nakamura, one of Kyoto's oldest and most prestigious kaiseki restaurants near Nishiki Market — reserve in advance for an authentic multi-course Kyoto cuisine experience

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Ask hotel concierge about cherry blossom bloom status and evening illumination schedules at Maruyama Park.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Experience hanami under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Arrive early morning (07:00–09:00) before crowds gather to enjoy the serene beauty. Walk to nearby Yasaka Shrine for a cultural morning blessing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Higashiyama Cultural District on foot — visit Kiyomizudera Temple (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), stroll the charming Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional shops and tea houses. Stop for matcha and wagashi sweets at a refined tea house.
day_by_day.evening: Evening illumination event at Maruyama Park and Kiyomizudera (if running during cherry blossom season). The lit-up weeping cherry tree and temple stage are among Japan's most magical sights.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at the hotel or nearby Omen Noodle House for a lighter start
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kasagi-ya, a historic sweet shop and tea house on Ninenzaka, followed by a full lunch at Hyotei (two-Michelin-star kaiseki) — book well in advance
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kikunoi Honten, a three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant in the Higashiyama area — seasonal cherry blossom-themed tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone lanes. Book Michelin-starred restaurants months in advance. Confirm evening illumination schedules with hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Arashiyama — take a private car or taxi (20 minutes from Gion). Walk through the iconic towering Arashiyama Bamboo Grove in the early morning for a tranquil, crowd-free experience. Visit Tenryuji Temple and its stunning Zen garden (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park for family fun — observe wild Japanese macaques with panoramic views of Kyoto. Return to Arashiyama and enjoy a rickshaw ride through the scenic riverside district. Explore Togetsukyo Bridge with cherry blossoms framing the mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion district. Attend a private maiko (apprentice geisha) performance or cultural experience arranged through the hotel — includes traditional dance, tea ceremony, and cultural Q&A.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before early departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shoraian, a riverside kaiseki restaurant in Arashiyama with beautiful garden views and seasonal cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mizai, a Michelin-starred restaurant in Fushimi serving refined Kyoto cuisine in an intimate setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the maiko cultural experience through the hotel concierge well in advance — these exclusive experiences are limited. Monkey Park requires a short uphill hike; wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — famous for its thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Start early (07:00) to avoid crowds. Hike the full trail or the lower section for spectacular views. Cherry blossoms may still be visible along the path.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for a premium food exploration — sample pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, grilled skewers, and Kyoto specialties. Afterward, visit the Kyoto National Museum for an immersive cultural experience featuring Japanese art, ceramics, and historical artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees, magical in late April. End the evening in the refined Okazaki district.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at hotel before shrine visit
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Nishiki Market — curated tasting of Kyoto delicacies, or sit-down lunch at Okutan Nanzenji, a 370-year-old tofu cuisine restaurant near Nanzenji Temple
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Sodoh Higashiyama Kyoto, a beautiful restaurant in a renovated artist's studio with garden views and contemporary Japanese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours — early morning visits are strongly recommended. The Philosopher's Path is at its most beautiful during cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day cultural immersion — begin with a private tea ceremony experience at Urasenke or a boutique tea house in Gion. Learn the art of Japanese tea from a certified tea master in an authentic tatami room setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace with its famous 'nightingale floors' and beautiful cherry blossom garden. Follow with a visit to Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion) for iconic golden reflections in the mirror pond.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit lane along the Kamo River with some of Kyoto's finest dining. In spring, many restaurants open their riverside 'kawayuka' terraces over the river.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at hotel — miso soup, grilled fish, rice, pickles, and tamagoyaki
meals.lunch: Lunch at Kichisen, a legendary three-Michelin-star kaiseki restaurant (reserve months ahead) or a refined bento lunch in the castle gardens
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kappa, a highly regarded restaurant on Pontocho Alley with seasonal kaiseki and riverside terrace seating

day_by_day.notes: The private tea ceremony can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Pontocho restaurants fill up quickly — make reservations in advance. Kawayuka terraces are typically open May onward but confirm dates.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hiroshima — take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Kyoto Station (approximately 1.5 hours). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Peace Memorial Park for a deeply moving and culturally significant experience. Pay respects at the Atomic Bomb Dome (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Hiroshima to Miyajima Island. Visit the iconic 'floating' Itsukushima Shrine and its famous torii gate rising from the sea. Walk the island's scenic paths, encounter friendly deer, and explore the Daisho-in Temple complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen. Quiet dinner near the hotel after a meaningful day.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before early Shinkansen departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Hiroshima — try Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake) at Okonomimura, a multi-floor okonomiyaki village
meals.dinner: Dinner at Oryori Hana, a refined Kyoto cuisine restaurant near Gion — intimate, seasonal, and elegant

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Shinkansen tickets in advance via the Japan Rail Pass or through the hotel concierge. The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. Allow 4–5 hours on Miyajima Island.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo by Shinkansen (approximately 2.5 hours from Kyoto). Check in to a luxury Tokyo hotel (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Freshen up and head to Tsukiji Outer Market for a premium food tour — sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and seasonal delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum (Azabudai Hills location) — immerse the family in breathtaking interactive digital art installations. This world-class experience is especially magical for children and adults alike, with light, sound, and movement creating an otherworldly environment.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Ginza district for luxury shopping and evening ambiance. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery and lifestyle store, or browse the high-end boutiques along Chuo-dori Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on board or at Kyoto hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Premium sushi lunch at Tsukiji Outer Market — sit-down omakase at a top sushi counter such as Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early or book ahead)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) — one of the world's most celebrated sushi restaurants (requires reservation months in advance) or Quintessence, a three-Michelin-star French-Japanese fusion restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets online well in advance as they sell out quickly. Tsukiji Outer Market is best experienced in the morning when produce is freshest. Confirm hotel check-in time for Tokyo property.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's largest and most beautiful parks, with over 1,000 cherry trees (late-blooming varieties may still be in flower in mid-April). A peaceful family-friendly morning of hanami in a manicured landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Harajuku and Omotesando area — visit Meiji Jingu Shrine for a serene cultural experience in a forested sanctuary. Walk along Omotesando Boulevard, Tokyo's most elegant shopping street, for luxury boutiques and architecture. Takeshita Street offers fun, colorful experiences for families.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend the Tokyo Skytree or Tokyo Tower for panoramic night views of the city. Enjoy the illuminated skyline stretching to Mount Fuji on clear evenings.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Western or Japanese set menu
meals.lunch: Lunch at Maisen Aoyama, a beloved premium tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant in a converted bathhouse near Omotesando
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ryugin, a three-Michelin-star restaurant in Roppongi specializing in innovative Japanese cuisine with seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small entry fee and prohibits alcohol — it is a refined, family-friendly alternative to Ueno Park. Book Ryugin well in advance. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line limited express or Shinkansen to Utsunomiya). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine — an extraordinarily ornate mausoleum complex set in a cedar forest. Explore the Rinno-ji Temple and Futarasan Shrine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, and enjoy the lush mountain scenery of Nikko National Park. Visit Lake Chuzenji for stunning alpine views. Return to Tokyo by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — explore the vibrant Shibuya crossing (the world's busiest pedestrian scramble) and Shibuya Sky observation deck. Farewell dinner at a world-class restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before early departure
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at Gyoshintei, a refined restaurant near Toshogu Shrine set in a beautiful garden — Nikko's local specialty
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Yebisu Garden Place) — legendary French-Japanese haute cuisine in an elegant château setting, or Sushi Yoshitake (three Michelin stars) for a final omakase experience

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko Pass for convenient round-trip travel and local bus access. Nikko can be busy on weekends — a Friday visit is ideal. Reserve the farewell dinner restaurant well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — visit the serene Hamarikyu Gardens, a historic tidal garden in the heart of the city, for a peaceful farewell stroll. Take a traditional wooden ferry across the Sumida River for a scenic perspective of Tokyo. Visit the Asakusa district and the iconic Senso-ji Temple for last-minute cultural immersion and souvenir shopping along Nakamise-dori.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to hotel for checkout and luggage collection. Private transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow ample time for international departure — arrive at least 3 hours before flight. Enjoy premium airport lounges (ANA Suite Lounge or JAL First Class Lounge) for a refined send-off.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of cherry blossoms, Michelin-starred kaiseki, ancient temples, and family adventures through one of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast at the hotel — savor every last bite of miso soup, grilled fish, and fresh rice
meals.lunch: Lunch at a celebrated tempura restaurant in Asakusa — Daikokuya Tempura, a 120-year-old institution, or Tempura Uchitsu for a premium tempura omakase
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport lounge or on board — premium airline dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow generous time for airport transfer from central Tokyo — Narita is 60–90 minutes away, Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Purchase any remaining gifts or Japanese snacks at the airport's excellent duty-free shops. Keep a small amount of yen for last-minute purchases as some vendors are cash-only.
